US House Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker
November 18, 2026
Jeffries is set to be the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives when Democrats take control of the chamber next year.
Democrats in the US House of Representatives on Wednesday nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be the next speaker.
Jeffries, who represents a district in New York, would be the first Black person to fill the role. He received 251 out of 265 ballots cast in a closed-door, secret vote.
Hakeem will begin his tenure as speaker in January, when Democrats take the majority in the chamber. The entire House will do a roll call vote on January 3, 2027 to elect Jeffries when the new Congress convenes.
Democrats won the House and the US Senate during the midterms earlier this month in a rebuke of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party. Democrats will have at least 257 seats in the House and 56 seats in the Senate.
Jeffries will steer Democratic priorities in the House, such as possible legislation and investigations of the Trump administration. He will also be second in line to the presidency after Vice President JD Vance.
